deepDive.title: Heart chambers + double circulation in detail
deepDive.body: Class 7 says heart has 4 chambers and 2 circulations. Class 9 details what each chamber does and WHY 4 chambers matter. RIGHT ATRIUM receives oxygen-poor blood from body veins. Contracts → blood drops to RIGHT VENTRICLE. Right ventricle pumps to lungs (low-pressure circuit — lungs are close). Lungs oxygenate, return blood to LEFT ATRIUM. Drops to LEFT VENTRICLE — the most muscular chamber. Left ventricle pumps to the WHOLE BODY (high-pressure — has to reach toes). Why 4 chambers? Fish (2 chambers) mix oxygenated + deoxygenated blood → inefficient. Amphibians (3 chambers) partially separate. Mammals/birds (4 chambers) — full separation, efficient, supports high metabolism. Why we're warm-blooded.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11 introduces cardiac cycle phases (systole/diastole) + valve operation timing.

deepDive.title: Transpiration pull — the physics of water rising 100 metres up a tree
deepDive.body: Class 7 says transpiration pulls water up plants. Class 11 reveals the physics. Water molecules cohere strongly (hydrogen bonds). When water evaporates from leaves' stomata, the water column in xylem behaves like a STRETCHED ROPE — every leaving molecule pulls up the column behind it. This is COHESION-TENSION THEORY. Negative pressure in xylem (yes, NEGATIVE — water under tension) can reach -2 MPa in tall trees. Atmospheric pressure can only push water up ~10 m (the pump physics) — but transpiration pull lifts redwoods 100+ m. Crucial: any AIR BUBBLE in xylem breaks the chain (embolism) — that branch dies. This is why drought stress is so dangerous; xylem embolisms are irreversible.
deepDive.nextStepHint: NEET tests cohesion-tension, root pressure, and adhesion to xylem walls.

deepDive.title: Nephron filtration math — how kidneys filter 180 litres a day
deepDive.body: Class 7 says nephrons filter blood. Class 10 makes it quantitative. Each kidney has ~1 million nephrons. Each filters ~125 mL of plasma per minute. That's 180 LITRES per day total — equivalent to filtering your entire blood volume 60 times. But you don't urinate 180 L! In the LOOP OF HENLE and convoluted tubules, ~99% is REABSORBED back to blood — water, glucose, salts, amino acids. Final urine: just 1.5 L/day. The reabsorption is selective: 100% glucose (unless diabetic), 99% water, varies by need for salts. Diuretics work by blocking specific reabsorption channels — water exits as urine instead of being kept. Indian dialysis patients lose this filtration — machines replace it at ~25% the efficiency.
deepDive.nextStepHint: JEE/NEET cover specific transporters in each tubule segment.
